easy.question: In which month must Passover be observed?
answers: In the month of Abib
In the month of Tishri
In the month of Kislev
easy.explanation: The verse commands Israel to observe the month of Abib and keep Passover then.

easy.question: What is eaten during the seven days of Passover?
answers: Leavened bread
Unleavened bread
Fruit only
easy.explanation: The verse says that unleavened bread is to be eaten for seven days.

easy.question: What must be done on the seventh day?
answers: Go to war
Offer another sacrifice
Hold a solemn assembly and do no work
easy.explanation: The seventh day is a solemn assembly to the Lord, and no work may be done.

medium.question: Why is unleavened bread eaten at Passover according to these verses?
answers: To remember the hurried departure from Egypt
To mark the beginning of summer
To celebrate the building of the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The unleavened bread recalls that the Israelites left Egypt in haste.

medium.question: In the phrase “you came forth out of Egypt in haste,” what does “in haste” mean?
answers: With great sadness
Quickly and urgently
After a long journey
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the Israelites leaving Egypt quickly and urgently.

medium.question: Where may the Passover sacrifice be offered?
answers: At any city gate
In each person’s home
At the place the Lord will choose
medium.explanation: The verses emphasize that Passover may be offered only at the place the Lord chooses.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the command that none of the Passover meat remain until morning?
answers: The meat should be eaten soon after it is offered
The meat may be saved for the following week
The meat must not be eaten in the evening
challenge.explanation: The command not to leave any meat until morning shows that it was to be eaten that night, not saved for another night.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Leaving in the morning, offering at noon, and eating at night
Offering in the evening, roasting and eating, then leaving in the morning
Eating in the morning, offering at noon, and staying there
challenge.explanation: The verses describe offering the sacrifice in the evening, roasting and eating it, and leaving for the tents in the morning.

challenge.question: What is the precise difference between the days mentioned in verse 3 and those mentioned in verse 8?
answers: Verse 3 says to eat leavened bread for seven days, while verse 8 says to eat unleavened bread for one day
Both verses say to eat unleavened bread for only five days
Verse 3 says to eat unleavened bread for seven days, while verse 8 emphasizes that the seventh day is a solemn assembly with no work
challenge.explanation: Verse 3 mentions eating unleavened bread for seven days, while verse 8 specifies that the seventh day is a solemn assembly on which no work may be done.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the command that none of the Passover meat remain until morning?
answers: The meat should be eaten soon after it is offered
The meat may be saved for the following week
The meat must not be eaten in the evening
questions.explanation: The command not to leave any meat until morning shows that it was to be eaten that night, not saved for another night.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Leaving in the morning, offering at noon, and eating at night
Offering in the evening, roasting and eating, then leaving in the morning
Eating in the morning, offering at noon, and staying there
questions.explanation: The verses describe offering the sacrifice in the evening, roasting and eating it, and leaving for the tents in the morning.

questions.question: What is the precise difference between the days mentioned in verse 3 and those mentioned in verse 8?
answers: Verse 3 says to eat leavened bread for seven days, while verse 8 says to eat unleavened bread for one day
Both verses say to eat unleavened bread for only five days
Verse 3 says to eat unleavened bread for seven days, while verse 8 emphasizes that the seventh day is a solemn assembly with no work
questions.explanation: Verse 3 mentions eating unleavened bread for seven days, while verse 8 specifies that the seventh day is a solemn assembly on which no work may be done.

paragraphs.title: The Feast of Weeks and Shared Joy

easy.question: How many weeks must be counted before the Feast of Weeks?
answers: Seven weeks
Three weeks
Ten weeks
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Seven weeks shalt thou number unto thee.”

easy.question: For whom is the Feast of Weeks celebrated?
answers: For the king
For the Lord your God
For the high priest
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt keep the feast of weeks unto the Lord thy God.”

easy.question: Who is commanded to rejoice with the worshiper?
answers: Only his family
Only the Levites
The stranger, the fatherless, and the widow as well
easy.explanation: The verse includes the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow among those who are to rejoice.

medium.question: When does the counting of the seven weeks begin?
answers: When the sickle is first put to the grain
At the beginning of Tishri
After the Feast of Tabernacles
medium.explanation: The count begins when the harvest starts and the sickle is first used on the grain.

medium.question: In the phrase “a tribute of a freewill offering of thine hand,” what does “tribute” mean?
answers: A tax or punishment
The amount or portion given
The location of the sanctuary
medium.explanation: Here, “tribute” means the amount or portion of the freewill offering, given according to the blessing the Lord has provided.

medium.question: Why are the Israelites reminded that they were slaves in Egypt?
answers: So they will remember their past and carefully observe the commandments
So they will return to work in Egypt
So they will celebrate without inviting others
medium.explanation: The verse connects remembering slavery in Egypt with observing and obeying God’s statutes.

challenge.question: What connection between the harvest and the Feast of Weeks appears in these verses?
answers: The feast takes place before any agricultural work begins
The counting begins with the harvest and leads to a thanksgiving offering to the Lord
The feast is meant to end the harvest permanently
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the beginning of the harvest, counting seven weeks, and bringing a freewill offering to the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the rejoicing takes place “at the place which the Lord thy God hath chosen”?
answers: Everyone must rejoice alone at home
The location of the celebration does not matter
The feast is connected with a central place chosen for worshiping the Lord
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the celebration takes place at the location chosen by the Lord, rather than privately anywhere.

challenge.question: What social principle is emphasized by the list of people commanded to rejoice?
answers: The feast should include vulnerable or disadvantaged people
Only wealthy people may take part in the feast
The Levites may not rejoice with the people
challenge.explanation: Along with family members, the list includes the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, emphasizing shared joy and care for those without land or support.

questions.question: What connection between the harvest and the Feast of Weeks appears in these verses?
answers: The feast takes place before any agricultural work begins
The counting begins with the harvest and leads to a thanksgiving offering to the Lord
The feast is meant to end the harvest permanently
questions.explanation: The verses connect the beginning of the harvest, counting seven weeks, and bringing a freewill offering to the Lord.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the rejoicing takes place “at the place which the Lord thy God hath chosen”?
answers: Everyone must rejoice alone at home
The location of the celebration does not matter
The feast is connected with a central place chosen for worshiping the Lord
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the celebration takes place at the location chosen by the Lord, rather than privately anywhere.

questions.question: What social principle is emphasized by the list of people commanded to rejoice?
answers: The feast should include vulnerable or disadvantaged people
Only wealthy people may take part in the feast
The Levites may not rejoice with the people
questions.explanation: Along with family members, the list includes the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, emphasizing shared joy and care for those without land or support.

paragraphs.title: The Feast of Tabernacles and the Joy of the Harvest

easy.question: How long does the Feast of Tabernacles last according to these verses?
answers: Seven days
Three days
Fourteen days
easy.explanation: The verses say that the Feast of Tabernacles is observed for seven days.

easy.question: When is the Feast of Tabernacles held according to verse 13?
answers: Before sowing
When the grain and wine are gathered in
At the beginning of winter
easy.explanation: The feast takes place after the harvest has been gathered from the threshing floor and winepress.

easy.question: What main feeling does the Torah command during the feast?
answers: Fear
Sorrow
Joy
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly emphasize rejoicing during the feast.

medium.question: Why does the Torah command rejoicing during the Feast of Tabernacles?
answers: Because no work is needed during the feast
Because the Lord has blessed the harvest and the work of their hands
Because the feast lasts only one day
medium.explanation: Verse 15 says that the people should rejoice because the Lord has blessed their produce and all the work of their hands.

medium.question: In the phrase “when thou hast gathered in thy corn and thy wine,” what does “gathered in” mean?
answers: Collected the harvest
Gone to war
Built a house
medium.explanation: “Gathered in” means collected the produce, here referring to grain and wine.

medium.question: Which combination correctly describes the feast in these verses?
answers: One day, at home, without rejoicing
Three days, in the wilderness, with fasting
Seven days, at the place the Lord chooses, with rejoicing
medium.explanation: The verses mention seven days, the place chosen by the Lord, and joyful celebration.

challenge.question: What does the list of participants reveal about the nature of the feast’s joy?
answers: The joy is for the whole community, including people who need support
The joy is only for landowners
The joy is only for priests
challenge.explanation: The list includes family members, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, presenting the celebration as shared and inclusive.

challenge.question: What detail in verse 15 broadens the source of blessing beyond the agricultural harvest?
answers: The mention of seven days
The mention of all the work of your hands
The mention of the place the Lord chooses
challenge.explanation: The verse speaks not only of produce but also of blessing in all the work of a person’s hands.

challenge.question: What is the connection between gathering the harvest and the command “thou shalt surely rejoice”?
answers: After seeing the blessing of his labor, a person should turn that blessing into joy before the Lord
A person rejoices only because the feast is short
Gathering the harvest removes the need to celebrate
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the completion of the harvest, recognition of the Lord’s blessing, and the command to rejoice.

questions.question: What does the list of participants reveal about the nature of the feast’s joy?
answers: The joy is for the whole community, including people who need support
The joy is only for landowners
The joy is only for priests
questions.explanation: The list includes family members, the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow, presenting the celebration as shared and inclusive.

questions.question: What detail in verse 15 broadens the source of blessing beyond the agricultural harvest?
answers: The mention of seven days
The mention of all the work of your hands
The mention of the place the Lord chooses
questions.explanation: The verse speaks not only of produce but also of blessing in all the work of a person’s hands.

questions.question: What is the connection between gathering the harvest and the command “thou shalt surely rejoice”?
answers: After seeing the blessing of his labor, a person should turn that blessing into joy before the Lord
A person rejoices only because the feast is short
Gathering the harvest removes the need to celebrate
questions.explanation: The verses connect the completion of the harvest, recognition of the Lord’s blessing, and the command to rejoice.

paragraphs.title: Three Pilgrimage Festivals and Giving According to One’s Means

easy.question: How many times each year must the people appear before the Lord?
answers: Three times
Twice
Once
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Three times in a year.”

easy.question: At which feasts must the people appear before the Lord?
answers: Passover, Rosh Hashanah, and Purim
The Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles
Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Hanukkah
easy.explanation: The verse names the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles.

easy.question: Where must they appear before the Lord?
answers: In their own homes
Anywhere they choose
At the place the Lord will choose
easy.explanation: The verse says they must appear at the place the Lord chooses.

medium.question: What can be understood from the command, “they shall not appear before the Lord empty”?
answers: It is not enough merely to arrive; a gift or offering must be brought
It is forbidden to enter the sanctuary
They must come only once a year
medium.explanation: The word “empty” shows that those who appear before the Lord should not come empty-handed.

medium.question: In the phrase “they shall not appear before the Lord empty,” what does “empty” mean?
answers: With great joy
Empty-handed, without a gift
From a distant place
medium.explanation: In this context, “empty” means without anything to bring as an offering.

medium.question: How does verse 17 explain the obligation not to appear before the Lord empty?
answers: Everyone must give exactly the same gift
Only the priests must bring a gift
Each person gives according to his ability and the blessing he has received
medium.explanation: The verse says that each person should give according to his ability and according to the blessing the Lord has given him.

challenge.question: What specific group is mentioned in the phrase “all thy males”?
answers: Males in particular
Children only
Priests only
challenge.explanation: The phrase explicitly identifies males as those commanded to appear before the Lord.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from the connection between “every man shall give as he is able” and “according to the blessing”?
answers: Rich and poor must give the same amount
Giving varies according to each person’s ability and blessing
No gift is needed if a person is joyful
challenge.explanation: The verse does not set one fixed amount; the gift is suited to each person’s ability and blessing.

challenge.question: What is the connection between appearing before the Lord three times and the command not to appear empty-handed?
answers: The command applies only during the Feast of Tabernacles
The gift replaces the pilgrimage to the chosen place
At each of the three pilgrimages, people must appear before the Lord with an appropriate gift
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the three pilgrimage festivals with the requirement to bring a gift, and the next verse explains that it should be according to one’s means.

questions.question: What specific group is mentioned in the phrase “all thy males”?
answers: Males in particular
Children only
Priests only
questions.explanation: The phrase explicitly identifies males as those commanded to appear before the Lord.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from the connection between “every man shall give as he is able” and “according to the blessing”?
answers: Rich and poor must give the same amount
Giving varies according to each person’s ability and blessing
No gift is needed if a person is joyful
questions.explanation: The verse does not set one fixed amount; the gift is suited to each person’s ability and blessing.

questions.question: What is the connection between appearing before the Lord three times and the command not to appear empty-handed?
answers: The command applies only during the Feast of Tabernacles
The gift replaces the pilgrimage to the chosen place
At each of the three pilgrimages, people must appear before the Lord with an appropriate gift
questions.explanation: The verse connects the three pilgrimage festivals with the requirement to bring a gift, and the next verse explains that it should be according to one’s means.

easy.question: Whom must the Israelites appoint in all their gates?
answers: Judges and officers
Kings and priests
Prophets and Levites
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates.”

easy.question: Where must judges and officers be appointed?
answers: Only in Jerusalem
Throughout all the gates of the land
Only near the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse commands that they be appointed in all the gates throughout the tribes.

easy.question: What kind of judgment must the judges administer?
answers: Quick judgment
Difficult judgment
Just judgment
easy.explanation: The verse says that they must judge the people with just judgment.

medium.question: Why does the Torah warn against taking bribes?
answers: Because a gift blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous
Because a bribe makes people leave the land
Because a bribe prevents judges from being appointed
medium.explanation: The verse explains that a gift can impair judgment and distort the words of righteous people.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt not respect persons,” what does “respect persons” mean?
answers: Failing to remember people’s names
Showing favoritism because of a person’s identity or status
Refusing to look at the litigants
medium.explanation: In a legal setting, the phrase means not favoring someone because of identity, appearance, or status.

medium.question: What is the main sequence of ideas in these verses?
answers: Inheriting the land, appointing judges, and accepting bribes
Accepting bribes, appointing judges, and living in the land
Appointing judges, forbidding biased judgment, and pursuing justice
medium.explanation: The passage first commands the appointment of judges, then forbids injustice and bribery, and finally commands the pursuit of justice.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the repetition in “justice, justice shalt thou follow”?
answers: Justice must be pursued persistently and in every situation
There are only two kinds of justice
Only judges need to be just
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the great importance of justice and the need to pursue it continually.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the pairing of “judges and officers”?
answers: Every person must be both a judge and an officer
Both those who decide cases and those who help enforce the decisions are needed
Officers may change the judges’ decisions
challenge.explanation: Judges decide cases, while officers help maintain order and enforce the law.

challenge.question: What connection does the verse make between pursuing justice and living in the land?
answers: Justice is required only after the land has been inherited
Those who pursue justice do not need laws
Pursuing justice is connected with living in and inheriting the land
challenge.explanation: The verse says, “that thou mayest live, and inherit the land,” linking justice with life in and possession of the land.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the repetition in “justice, justice shalt thou follow”?
answers: Justice must be pursued persistently and in every situation
There are only two kinds of justice
Only judges need to be just
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the great importance of justice and the need to pursue it continually.

questions.question: What can be understood from the pairing of “judges and officers”?
answers: Every person must be both a judge and an officer
Both those who decide cases and those who help enforce the decisions are needed
Officers may change the judges’ decisions
questions.explanation: Judges decide cases, while officers help maintain order and enforce the law.

questions.question: What connection does the verse make between pursuing justice and living in the land?
answers: Justice is required only after the land has been inherited
Those who pursue justice do not need laws
Pursuing justice is connected with living in and inheriting the land
questions.explanation: The verse says, “that thou mayest live, and inherit the land,” linking justice with life in and possession of the land.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of Asherah Poles and Sacred Images beside the Altar

easy.question: What may not be planted beside the altar of the Lord?
answers: An Asherah pole or any tree
A grapevine
Wheat
easy.explanation: The verse forbids planting an Asherah pole or any tree beside the altar of the Lord.

easy.question: What may not be set up according to verse 22?
answers: An altar
An image or sacred pillar
A house
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Neither shalt thou set thee up any image.”

easy.question: Who hates the sacred image?
answers: The people
The priest
The Lord your God
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord your God hates it.

medium.question: Why is planting an Asherah pole or a tree beside the Lord’s altar forbidden?
answers: To keep foreign worship practices away from the place of worship
To save space
To protect the trees
medium.explanation: The prohibition distinguishes worship of the Lord from symbols and practices associated with foreign worship.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt not plant thee an Asherah,” what is an Asherah?
answers: A musical instrument
A tree or ritual symbol associated with idolatry
A type of altar
medium.explanation: The context of planting it beside the altar indicates that an Asherah was a tree or ritual symbol associated with idolatrous worship.

medium.question: Which sequence correctly describes the two prohibitions?
answers: First setting up an image, then planting an Asherah
First allowing a tree, then forbidding an altar
First planting an Asherah or tree, then setting up an image
medium.explanation: Verse 21 concerns planting an Asherah or tree, while verse 22 concerns setting up an image.

challenge.question: In the phrase “the altar of the Lord thy God, which thou shalt make thee,” what does “which thou shalt make thee” describe?
answers: Any tree
The altar of the Lord
The Asherah
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the altar that a person might make, not the Asherah or the tree.

challenge.question: What do the Asherah and the sacred image have in common in these two verses?
answers: Both are forms of worship that the Lord forbids beside his altar
Both are types of sacrifices
Both are parts of the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: Both verses forbid placing religious symbols associated with idolatry alongside the worship of the Lord.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the prohibitions are directed at the individual?
answers: The word “hates”
The words “for yourself”
The word “any”
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording “for yourself” emphasizes that a person may not create or set up these objects for personal use.

questions.question: In the phrase “the altar of the Lord thy God, which thou shalt make thee,” what does “which thou shalt make thee” describe?
answers: Any tree
The altar of the Lord
The Asherah
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the altar that a person might make, not the Asherah or the tree.

questions.question: What do the Asherah and the sacred image have in common in these two verses?
answers: Both are forms of worship that the Lord forbids beside his altar
Both are types of sacrifices
Both are parts of the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Both verses forbid placing religious symbols associated with idolatry alongside the worship of the Lord.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that the prohibitions are directed at the individual?
answers: The word “hates”
The words “for yourself”
The word “any”
questions.explanation: The repeated wording “for yourself” emphasizes that a person may not create or set up these objects for personal use.
